item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
• Half the download. Squish is now a 20 MB download (was 42 MB) and takes 52 MB on disk (was 85 MB).
  • Fixed: adding lots of files at once. Dropping more than 64 files could leave every row stuck on "Reading". Large folders now load quickly, in name order.
  • Lighter on your Mac. With the default Fastest encoder, H.264 and HEVC videos kept at their original size now decode on the media engine too: same result, much less CPU.
  • Quicker previews and estimates. The live preview appears about twice as fast, and estimates only rerun when a setting that affects the result changes.
  • More accurate "By file size" previews. They now show the quality the finished file will really have.
  • A denser queue. Rows are about 30% shorter, so more files fit, and the queue and settings share the window more evenly.
  • Easier to read. Better contrast in light mode, smoother progress rings, and steadier rows on hover.
  • New sounds. A softer chime when a batch finishes, a small pluck when you drop files in, and a low two-note sound if a batch fails. Turn them off in Settings › General › Sounds.

item.title: Version 0.2.3
item.description:
• Squish again. After a batch finishes, you no longer need to clear the queue to run another pass. Change your settings and the button becomes Squish again, re-encoding the finished files. Earlier files are kept, and new ones get a numbered name.
  • You can also squish a single finished file again from its row (hover, or right-click), or by dropping it onto the window again.

item.title: Version 0.2.2
item.description:
• Updates from inside Squish. From now on Squish checks for new versions about once a day and installs them in one click, with no approval step. You can also use Squish › Check for Updates…, or turn checking off in Settings › General › Updates.
  • Vertical video previews. The small before/after preview now shows the whole frame for vertical and square video, instead of cropping it to widescreen.
